_README: DISCLOSED-RESIDUAL allowlist for migrate.ts's assertAppliedHashMatches() sha256 guard (Dvārapāla RULING 58/67's guard; the file-content-drift class, NOT the migration_number_guard.ts duplicate-number class — see migration_number_legacy_duplicates.json for that sibling mechanism, same discipline). RULING 73: on migrate.ts's first live deploy run, 16 already-applied migrations were found whose on-disk sha256 no longer matches the sha256 recorded in production's `_migrations_applied` at apply time — a real historical data-integrity gap the guard is CORRECTLY catching, not a guard bug. Reverting the guard was explicitly rejected (it would neuter a control that just proved its value); blind reconciliation of 16 undocumented historical edits under deploy-pipeline pressure was explicitly PARKED, not attempted (Ruling 73's 'Option 2', a genuine future lane). This file freezes the 16 known-mismatch (stored, current) hash PAIRS as of the disclosure date. Each entry pins the EXACT stored sha256 (from `_migrations_applied.sha256`) and the EXACT current on-disk sha256 as of RULING 73 — assertAppliedHashMatches() passes a disclosed file through with a visible non-fatal warning ONLY when BOTH pinned values match exactly what it observes live. The disclosure pins one specific historical mismatch; it is NOT a standing exemption — if the file is edited AGAIN after this disclosure (current on-disk hash no longer equals `current_sha256_at_disclosure`), the guard fails loudly exactly as it would for an undisclosed file. Same itemized/dated/attributed discipline as `migration_number_legacy_duplicates.json`'s `disclosed_additions` and `schema_validator.py`'s `known_residuals` whitelist: exit-clean iff ITEMIZED, never a blanket pass — an entry missing a required field is treated as UNDISCLOSED.
investigation_note: Ruling 73 asked whether commit 751ce3b8 ('fix(migrations): seed all 86 pre-tracking legacy migration files into _migrations_applied', 2026-06-22) explains some or all of the 16. Verified via `git log --follow` per file plus a full-history blob search (`git rev-list --all --objects`, all branches/tags) comparing each historical revision's sha256 against the stored production value. Finding: 751ce3b8 explains exactly ONE of the 16 — 0000_seed_legacy_applied.sql itself, which it directly edited 9 minutes after that file was applied to production. It does NOT explain any of the other 15; each of those traces to a DIFFERENT cause, itemized per-entry below. Four distinct causal classes found, none guessed: (1) a later, unrelated commit edited an already-applied file (0000_seed_legacy_applied.sql, 250, 358, 370 — each pinned to the exact prior commit whose content matches the stored hash and the exact later commit that changed it); (2) a single bulk pre-tracking seed action on 2026-06-05 stored 32-hex-character (MD5-length, not SHA-256) values for 4 files, an algorithm mismatch at seed time that can never match sha256Of() regardless of content (v13_pyramid_layers, 158_classical_texts_schema, ws2_l0_ontology, 002_ganita_divisionals); (3) four individually-dated manual/direct INSERTs via Cloud SQL Auth Proxy stored descriptive placeholder strings instead of hashes, bypassing sha256Of() entirely (215, 229, 231, 322); (4) four files (237, 294, 314, 377) have a well-formed 64-hex SHA-256 stored value but NO blob matching it exists anywhere in git history reachable from any branch or tag — the applied-time content was never committed under this filename. Marked UNDER-INVESTIGATION per Ruling 73's instruction not to fabricate a cause.

SAMAPTI 2026-07-30, RESOLVED-AS-IMMATERIAL (was UNDER-INVESTIGATION). Effect verified live: to_regclass('public.signal_type_registry') IS NULL — the table is gone, which is the migration's entire executable content (a single 'DROP TABLE IF EXISTS signal_type_registry CASCADE;'). Any variant of this file that produced the observed state contained that statement, so the drift is confined to the non-executable header commentary and a fresh replay of the on-disk file reproduces production exactly. REPLAY-EQUIVALENT. Origin of the exact applied bytes remains UNRECOVERABLE: swept all 68,303 objects in the repository object database (22,112 blobs, reachable AND dangling, under EVERY filename, plus LF-normalisation) — no blob hashes to the stored value. Also ruled out as benign-mechanical: no line-ending (LF/CRLF/CR), BOM, trailing-newline, trailing-whitespace, tab/space or latin-1 re-encode transform of the committed content reproduces the stored hash, and no alternate digest (md5/sha1/sha224/sha384/sha512/sha3-256/blake2s) over it does either. Root-cause CLASS is nonetheless now established and is shared by all four: in every case applied_at PRECEDES the file's only commit (by 11s to 2h57m), so the content applied was working-tree content that was edited before it was committed — for 237 the commit message itself says 'migration 237 applied to prod; to_regclass -> NULL confirmed', i.e. the file was applied by hand and its header then written up. What is UNKNOWN is only the exact bytes; what the migration DID is verified below.

round_2_investigation_note: ROUND 1 (PR #941, merged 3e05ef17) pinned 16 mismatches but its candidate enumeration missed 17 additional rows in _migrations_applied that are not 64-character-hex SHA-256 values -- some MD5-length (32 hex chars), some free-text sentinels ('manual', 'applied-2026-06-16').
